tagline: The Garden Isle's resort coasts and the sea-only Nā Pali coast — a premium, low-impact water layer for a fragile, road-limited island.
summary: Kauaʻi concentrates visitor demand on the south (Poʻipū), east (Līhuʻe / Nāwiliwili) and north (Princeville / Hanalei) coasts, with the legendary Nā Pali coast accessible only by sea and only in calm season. The island's single-road geography and chronic north-shore congestion at Hanalei make a quiet, low-wake water layer attractive — and Kauaʻi's strict environmental sensitivity rewards a zero-emission, low-wake foiling profile over conventional craft. Nāwiliwili is the commercial harbor and the Quanta-LR endpoint of the Kauaʻi Channel line-haul to Oʻahu.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the intra-island layer: south-shore transfers, the north-shore congestion bypass, and the seasonal Nā Pali tour.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) carries the ~72 nm Kauaʻi Channel line-haul to Oʻahu.

competitive_landscape: Inter-island air serves Līhuʻe; the Nā Pali catamaran tour fleet is the incumbent marine operator. Strict environmental review and seasonal north-shore swell shape operations — a low-wake, zero-emission profile is the differentiator.
seasonality: South shore is calmer in winter; north shore and Nā Pali are accessible mainly in the calm summer season — a clear operating-window discipline.
regulatory_note: Kauaʻi has some of the strictest environmental and shoreline rules in Hawaii; a zero-emission, low-wake foiling profile aligns directly. US Coast Guard Subchapter T applies; Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors controls Nāwiliwili and Port Allen.
